concept.title: Label Check: Protein Mix
concept.big_idea: A split-screen label walk-through in her clinical setting, in the style of her packaged-product review posts. She reads the Little Joys Proteinmix label lines as printed, and sends parents back to their child's doctor for serving questions.
concept.objective: Attention-stage creative test with this creator. A hypothesis, not a prediction: organic results do not predict paid performance.
why_fit: Creative DNA: Across 20 posts: formats piece to camera (95%), voiceover montage (5%); content expert explainer (95%), tutorial (5%); language english (100%); settings clinical (100%); children on camera 85%; product shown 45%; sponsored 10%.

heavy on explainer / piece to camera (95% of posts): Talking-to-camera is this creator's default; in Little Joys ads it had LOWER hook rates, so test an opening visual or story beat before the explanation. Caution: Post label is broader than the ad label.

Child visible on screen (85% of posts): Build the brief around the creator's own child in the product's routine moment (breakfast, tiffin, milk time). Caution: Ads: the strongest signal is a child in the FIRST 3 s, which posts cannot show (no timing label).
Attention alignment score 14/100 (AI-labelled posts vs paid-ad hook-rate patterns; organic engagement is not treated as evidence of paid performance).

tone.summary: Fast, reassuring and clinical: a doctor teaching label literacy, with Hindi explanation and English terms.
delivery: Pace: quick and energetic, as in her posts, but slow down for quoted label lines.
Language: Hindi explanation with English product and label terms (English-only would feel foreign).
Direct 'aap' address, split-screen layout, 'Save this reel' close.
Teach how to read a label; never recommend the product or a dose.
tone.creator_voice_in_profile: She speaks in a fast, energetic, and professional manner, primarily using Hindi with English medical terminology. Her tone is consistently reassuring and clinical.
tone.catchphrases_in_profile: Direct 'aap' address to the viewer; Call to action 'Save this reel'; Use of a medical doll for physical demonstrations; Split-screen visual layout
tone.native_in_profile: A video featuring the doctor in her clinical setting or a clean, bright space, using a split-screen format to explain the science behind a product's safety or efficacy.

avoid.item: Any claim that the product treats, prevents or cures anything, or improves immunity, growth, height, weight, brain development or strength.
avoid.reason: No such claim is verified in the supplied files; several older ads contain them (see restricted claims list).

avoid.item: Any number, percentage, multiplier or vitamin count that is not one of the verified product facts for the chosen product.
avoid.reason: Numeric claims must trace to a fact ID.

avoid.item: Superlatives and exclusivity ("best", "only", "No. 1", "bestseller", "loved by 10 lakh moms").
avoid.reason: Appear in older ad copy but cannot be substantiated from the files.

avoid.item: Comparisons with, or mentions of, other brands or products.
avoid.reason: Competitor kids-nutrition brands appear in several shortlisted creators' sponsored posts; keep the Little Joys video clean of them.

avoid.item: Third-party testing or certification claims (e.g. lab tested, Eurofins).
avoid.reason: Mentioned in ad copy, but certificates are not part of the supplied files.

avoid.item: Scripted taste or eating outcomes ("kids love it", "finishes it in two minutes"). Film real reactions only.
avoid.reason: Outcome claims are unverified; scripted reactions would misrepresent what happened.

avoid.item: "Doctor recommended", "expert approved" or any medical-authority endorsement the creator has not personally confirmed.
avoid.reason: Endorsement must be genuine and disclosed.

avoid.item: Age suitability, serving size or dosage statements unless supplied by Little Joys.
avoid.reason: Not available in the supplied files; left as [[CONFIRM: ...]] placeholders.
Every script ends with a disclosure line; confirm the platform's disclosure label.

avoid.item: English-only audio or a scripted sales pitch without medical context (flagged as foreign to her style).
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Stating or implying that any child needs protein supplementation, or recommending a dose; her authority makes this high-stakes.
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Product-review language that ranks Little Joys against other brands; her review posts name other brands.
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Other brands visible in this creator's posts (AI-labelled): Alkem, Calpol, Carepure, Chupa Chups, Cipla, Dr. Reddy's, Ibugesic Plus, LifeCell, Meftal, Woodwards. Do not show or mention any in the Little Joys video.
avoid.reason: Exclusivity and clean-brand framing; verify contracts.

avoid.item: Foreign-feeling styles per profile: High-production studio lighting, scripted sales pitches that lack medical context, or English-only audio without Hindi explanations.
